items.name: THE ILLINOIS
items.caption: A city in the sky. A mile above Chicago. Still only on paper.
items.why_unbuilt: Wright had no secured site, client, or budget for his mile-high tower.
items.what_remains: Drawings and later visualisations preserve the ambition of a vertical city.
items.note: Announced in 1956 as a 528-storey, mile-high tower. It was a conceptual proposal, not a funded construction project. Artwork is an AI-generated interpretation; skyline and details are illustrative.
items.image_alt: Artistic reconstruction of THE ILLINOIS in monochrome engraving style.

items.name: FORD NUCLEON
items.caption: The car of tomorrow had a reactor in the back. Tomorrow never arrived.
items.why_unbuilt: The concept depended on nuclear reactors becoming small, light, and safe enough for an everyday car.
items.what_remains: A non-working 3/8-scale model and Ford brochures preserve this atomic-age vision.
items.note: The museum describes the Nucleon as more a public-relations exercise than serious development. Only a non-functional model was built; there was no running nuclear car. Artwork interprets the styling concept.
items.image_alt: Artistic reconstruction of FORD NUCLEON in monochrome engraving style.

items.name: PROJECT ORION
items.caption: A spaceship riding nuclear explosions. The future had a fallout problem.
items.why_unbuilt: Nuclear-test restrictions, fallout concerns, and withdrawn government support ended the programme.
items.what_remains: Design studies and a conventional-explosive test model survive; the nuclear spacecraft was never built.
items.note: *Period refers to the research programme. A December 1964 memo records support ending on 31 December; Smithsonian dates cancellation to 1965. Small models used conventional explosives. Artwork is a conceptual interpretation, not a specific final design.
